corrections.claim: Serious, 02_chat.png: 'Repeated letters are the same outline, not a variant of it' - all seven isolated 't' components match one prototype at IoU 0.798-1.000 with a median outline-to-outline distance of 0.00 px, and 'the hero shows exactly one form of t repeated six times across four notes'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The three 't' components the report names by coordinate (x=535, 641, 771 at y=405) are not one rasterisation. Best integer-shift IoU between them is 0.778, 0.862 and 0.863; upsampled 8x and aligned to an eighth of a pixel, the residual between them is 3.54, 4.36 and 4.83 grey levels, where the same glyph shifted by half a pixel through the identical pipeline gives 0.00. Both hands carry five distinct 't' outlines (t, t.v1..t.v4; every pair differs in the outline record) behind calt/rand, and in TeoHand two DIFFERENT variants of 't' score up to IoU 0.844 against each other - so 0.86 between two screen t's does not separate 'same outline' from 'different variant'. evidence/logs/fonts.json, which this report lists as opened, states the expected collision rate outright: five variants per glyph, twins.share 0.3006 against a floor of 0.2, ok true. The repeats seen are that collision rate, not one outline.

corrections.claim: Serious, 02_chat.png: '53 of the 148 handwritten letter components on the screen (35.8 per cent, delivery ticks excluded) fall into 22 groups that are pixel-identical at IoU >= 0.90.'
corrections.what_i_measured: On the same still I find 447 letter-sized ink components on paper; 100 of them (22.4 per cent) have a twin at best-shift IoU >= 0.90 and 203 (45.4 per cent) at >= 0.85. No handwritten pair is pixel-identical: the only three exactly equal masks are 6x32 solid bars at y=140-141, which are the dial strokes in the standing banner, not letters. 'Pixel-identical at IoU >= 0.90' is also two different claims in one phrase. Separately and unremarked: evidence/logs/hand.json, listed as opened by this report, gives 31 of 511 marks with a twin (twin_share 0.061) at IoU 0.85 and a best-fit maximum of 0.97 - six times lower, and flatly inconsistent with 'pixel-identical' - and the report never says the two disagree.

corrections.claim: Serious, 10_first_run.png: the desk's high-frequency power across the grain is 0.2 per cent of the power along it (median ratio 0.002, p90 0.018; 0.003 in 02_chat and 01_pulse) against 0.53-0.60 for blank paper.
corrections.what_i_measured: Same measure (3 px high-pass, Hann window, second-moment minor/major eigenvalue ratio of the power spectrum above a 6-cycle cutoff, on 128 px tiles wholly inside each surface): desk median 0.062 on 10_first_run, 0.062 on 02_chat, 0.057 on 01_pulse; paper 0.509, 0.515, 0.492. The paper half reproduces; the desk is about 6 per cent across-to-along, not 0.2 per cent - roughly thirty times less anisotropic than reported. The direction stands. Two things also worth saying against the severity: assets/MANIFEST.json names blender/shell/desk.py as the generator, so the desk is a Blender render, which is the class of thing the row explicitly accepts for folds; and the row's named subjects are stock, tear masks, folds, handwriting, feeling objects and contact shadows, none of which is the desk.

corrections.claim: Minor, 03_us.png: one torn silhouette used twice - the two wide strips' bottom edges agree to a mean absolute difference of 0.28 px over 1269 columns at a lag of 1 px (NCC 0.978) on a roughness of only 2.1 px rms.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, crops/reception.png: 'Nothing in the evidence shows a message announcing itself while the app is closed ... records: [] ... a notification actually appearing is proved nowhere, on any browser.'
corrections.what_i_measured: Reproduced, and it is the build's behaviour rather than the harness's. crops/reception.png and crops/reception_replaced.png are byte-identical (md5 2b33b0bba0c0f7028f7421d7a9b8afc1, sha256 4677957956d2526f...), both an about:blank Chromium window on a black X root; crops/reception_open.png, taken after a push with the app still in front, shows no banner either; logs/reception.json records `records: []`. I then ran the harness's own path myself - xvfb-run -s '-screen 0 1180x1100x24', the repo's Playwright Chromium, a worker registered at /push/, CDP ServiceWorker.deliverPushMessage, the page navigated to about:blank, then getNotifications() from a document on the same origin. A minimal worker records {title 'noor', body 'left something', tag 'from-them'}. The build's own app/web/push/sw.js, served unchanged through the same script, records []. The cause is two adjacent lines: sw.js:121-122 passes `silent: true` together with `vibrate: ARRIVAL` whenever the treatment is `interrupt`, and Chromium rejects that pair - TypeError: 'Silent notifications must not specify vibration patterns.' I isolated it with a worker differing only in that field: `interrupt` rejects and shows nothing, `quiet` (where vibrate is undefined) shows the notification. `interrupt` is the default when no preference is stored and is the treatment 05_settings.png shows for a feeling ('a feeling / wake me'), so the loudest class of arrival is exactly the one that never appears. No report in the cycle names this; the finding is understated, not overstated.

corrections.claim: Serious, 11_chat_scroll.mp4: 777 frames, over_16ms 777; build_ms p50 5, p75 43, p90 730, p95 773, max 1109; 187 of 777 frames over 100 ms, arriving every 3 to 6 frames and spread evenly (49, 48, 49, 41 per 200); raster p50 117, max 200.
corrections.what_i_measured: Every number is exact - 777, 777, 5, 43, 730, 773, 1109, 117, 200, 187, and 49/48/49/41, with inter-arrival gaps of 3, 4, 5 and 6 frames. Three qualifications the report does not make. The 777 frames are the whole scene's FrameTiming record (the `timings` step reads window.__deskTimings, and logs/11_chat_scroll.json shows goTo, scrollTo and settle before the grab), while the clip is 300 frames, so 'the whole fling - seven throws ... 777 frames' runs two windows together. `over_16ms: 777` carries no signal: raster alone is 117 ms at the median on a GPU-less headless WebKit, so every frame is over budget by construction. And the cost is not a harness stall bleeding into build - build and raster are uncorrelated (r = 0.03) - but neither is it the smooth per-row layout cost described: the distribution is hard bimodal, 587 frames under 50 ms and 186 over 600 ms with three frames in the entire 50-600 ms band, which is a fixed-cost blocking operation firing per new sheet.

gaps: NOBODY TOOK THE ONE FINDING THAT EXPLAINS THE BLOCKING ONE. app/web/push/sw.js:121-122 sends `silent: true` and `vibrate: ARRIVAL` in the same showNotification call whenever the treatment is `interrupt`; Chromium rejects the pair outright ('Silent notifications must not specify vibration patterns'), the awaited promise fails inside the push handler where nothing catches it, and no notification is created. I proved it three ways in the harness's own environment: a minimal worker records a notification, the build's own sw.js records none, and a worker differing only in that field shows one under `quiet` and none under `interrupt`. `interrupt` is the default with no stored preference and the treatment 05_settings.png shows for a feeling, so of the fourteen announceable event types the six most urgent - message, photo, video, voice_note, feeling, ping - are precisely the ones that announce nothing. This is a two-line defect that has survived seven cycles because no rubric row owns the push path: messenger_reliability reaches it only through 'a reason to open Instagram' and emotional_transmission only through 'perceptible without opening the app', and the code critic's nine rules do not mention it.

TWO DOCUMENTS IN THIS CYCLE GIVE THE SAME MEASUREMENT SIX TIMES APART AND NEITHER SAYS SO. evidence/logs/hand.json reports 31 of 511 marks with a twin at IoU 0.85 (twin_share 0.061, best-fit maximum 0.97); material_truth reports 35.8 per cent of letter components twinned at IoU 0.90 and calls them pixel-identical; emotional_transmission cites the log's 0.061 approvingly in its not_worth_opening. My own count lands between them (22.4 per cent at 0.90, 45.4 per cent at 0.85 over 447 components) and finds no pixel-identical letter pair at all. The briefing singles hand.json out as a log to check against the pictures rather than trust; one critic contradicted it by six times without noticing, another took it at face value, and the cycle has no reconciled number for the thing its second-heaviest row turns on.

A FINDING THAT IS AN ARTIFACT OF THE CAPTURE, NOT THE BUILD. messenger_reliability's serious finding that 13_messenger_states.png 'loses the one it explicitly waited for' is the harness's wall clock beating a real-time timer: logs/13_messenger_states.json records `awaitView` at 9111 ms and `shot` at 3981 ms after the `far typing on` instruction - 13.1 seconds of wall clock against the six-second typing timer in app/lib/scope.dart:155-160. The briefing says in terms that the seconds between grabs are the harness's cost of taking the picture and not the app's. The artifact does lack the indicator and that is worth fixing in the scene; the build is not shown to drop typing, and typing is visible in every strip frame of 06 and 11, which the same report says.

THE EVIDENCE MOVED UNDER THE REVIEW, AND IS STILL MOVING. app/build/web was rebuilt at 23:21-23:22, between messenger_reliability (22:55) and coherence (23:26). evidence/reliability.json and evidence/coldstart.json carry mtimes of 23:35, the code critic having run the suite over them and restored them. app/lib/material/paper.dart changed at 23:52. chat_region.dart, spine.dart, voice/strings.dart and reliability_test.dart changed at 00:14 and a new test appeared at 00:16 - the fix for this cycle's first blocking finding, landing ten minutes after the last report. evidence/logs/reception_scene.json was rewritten again while I was reading it, with a new profile and a new `shown_by_the_worker: []` field. Six reports scored six different states of the tree, and none of them scored the one that exists now.

DIFF.JSON SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IT MEANS ON BOTH CHANGED ARTIFACTS. `label_basis` on 07_feeling_landing.mp4 (ssim 0.9866) and on 13_messenger_states.png (ssim 0.7088) both read 'ssim X against 0.999 - at or above it, nothing a person would see has moved'. Both are below it, which is why they are labelled `changed`; the sentence explains the case that did not happen. Its `labels` field also declares four labels - new, gone, unchanged, changed - and the file then uses a fifth, `absent`, twice, with a `counts` key for it, which left the coherence critic inventing a mapping for a label its instructions did not cover. Coherence quoted this file for both artifacts and neither it nor anyone else read the sentence.

THE CAPTURE RECORDS WHAT IS ON THE GLASS FOR SEVEN OF EIGHTEEN EVENT TYPES. Aggregating the `kinds` blocks across every scene report, the union of types the capture says appeared in any artifact is message, voice_note, video, feeling, state_declared, ritual_kept and todo_event. Eleven are never recorded anywhere: photo, reaction, message_edit, message_delete, read_marker, state_passive, date_event, milestone, passed_on, ping and feeling_authored. Several of them are visible by eye and messenger_reliability found them that way, but the record cannot be checked against the picture for any of the eleven. 04_moments.report.json - the media archive, the one screen whose whole subject is photos, video and voice notes - records neither `visible` nor `kinds` at all. Nobody asked for this and no row requires it.

NO RUBRIC ROW COVERS THE THIRD OF THE MISSION. The goal names a shared relationship OS with a date planner and tracker, shared to-do lists, anniversaries and calendar, rituals and streaks, ambient widgets and scheduled pings. Row 04 asks only whether a fifth module could be added without rework, and both critics answered that well. Nothing in the rubric asks whether the five that ship do their job: no critic looked at whether the date planner plans a date, whether the to-do list can be used, whether the calendar is right, or whether the shelf and rituals are pleasant. 03_us.png is the modules screen and it was read this cycle only for one visual language and for partner state. `ping` - the mission's scheduled pings - appears thirteen times in the seeded year, is registered as Notify.interruptive, is one of the five announceable types 05_settings.png does not reach, is caught by the sw.js defect above, and is named in no finding by anyone.

OTHER THINGS NO ROW OWNS: the push and notification path as such; onboarding and pairing as a journey two people complete (10_first_run.png and 17_setup_pwa.png are read for voice and for chrome, never for whether the pairing works); accessibility, contrast, text size and one-handed reach; the Android home-screen widget (android/.../Widget.kt, 270 lines of Kotlin, named only in passing by the code critic as a SharedPreferences blind spot); what happens to media and blobs at rest, or when a pairing is lost; and battery or resource cost on a real device.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW AT ALL. Nothing on Android: no artifact, no APK on disk, no widget. No haptic ever executed - logs/haptics.json's `channel_here` is 'page' for every capture, so the row's own test, a feeling identifiable by its pattern with the screen face down, cannot be run on any artifact in the set. No notification appearing, on any browser. No two devices in one frame: the far phone is `dart run tool/host_daemon.dart`, a screenless spine, so every arrival in 07, 08 and 15 enters as an injected line. The offline queue and reconnect ordering exist only as prose in reliability.json. The PWA has never been measured as an installed home-screen app - logs/pwa.json records `display_mode_standalone: false`, and standalone is the only mode in which iOS gives push at all, which is the exact case the iPhone substitute is scored on; emotional_transmission cited pwa.json for the service worker and nobody read that line. Media search returns no photo, video or voice note (12_search: hits 10, kinds message 8, ritual_kept 1, todo_event 1). No sent reply is rendered in any thread. The tailnet crossing in reliability.json and coldstart.json is dated 2026-09-05, four days before this capture, and both files carry `later_check: status pending, the nodes were not answering` - only the code critic mentioned this, and messenger_reliability cited reliability.json for ordering without noting that its transport half is four days old. And there is no picture of any screen during a seeded first launch, which is between 6.9 and 25.9 seconds long.

A SMALLER ONE, ON HOW THE REVIEW WAS CONDUCTED: three of the six reports say a task list or a sibling report surfaced unbidden in their session and that they did not read into it. That is the right disclosure and I mention it only because it happened three times out of six, which suggests the isolation the briefing depends on is leaking rather than each critic being unlucky.
verdict:
Coverage this cycle is genuinely good and the last completeness pass's complaint has been answered: no file under evidence/ went both unopened and undeclined, every present artifact was read by at least three critics, and the declines are argued rather than silent. The thin spot is evidence/scenes/, which fifteen of seventeen times nobody opened - and it is the one place a reader can tell a driven artifact from a staged one, which matters because 13_messenger_states, the still the cycle's only blocking picture-finding rests on, has a `stage` step in its script. I checked it; the staging is real emission down the real path and the refusal is the host's own, which is a fact about the build that the review never established for itself.

On the numbers, most of what was measured holds. Every figure in messenger_reliability's scroll finding reproduces to the digit; the fling log's asked-equals-moved is exact; the coherence critic's pixel-identical top bands and tab strips are exact; the emotional critic's tremor timings reproduce and are in fact a frame tighter than reported; 04_moments' undated voice notes, the 401 in 14_media_viewer, the search hit breakdown, the cold-start times, the `2s` against `0:03`, the seventeen-versus-eighteen in types.dart:1, the module_costs substring guard against the pairing vocabulary, the assert-free zz_probe test, the three internet fonts in the bundle, the absence of any `flutter test` in the repo - all of it stands. The 03_us tear repeat stands and is tighter than reported: NCC 0.994 at lag 0, nine hundredths of a pixel over 1269 columns, against a control of 0.055.

Three things do not survive being measured again. The heaviest is material_truth's handwriting finding, which is wrong in its central claim: the three 't's it names by coordinate are not one outline - they differ by three and a half to five grey levels after sub-pixel alignment, where an identical glyph gives zero - both hands carry five distinct 't' outlines behind calt, and in TeoHand two different variants score IoU 0.844 against each other, so the 0.80-0.86 it measured cannot tell 'same outline' from 'different variant'. evidence/logs/fonts.json, which that report lists as opened, already states the expected collision rate at 0.3006 against a floor of 0.2 and passes it. Its twin-share figure is overstated as well, and it sits six times above evidence/logs/hand.json's number for the same thing with neither document acknowledging the other. Second, the desk anisotropy is about 6 per cent across-to-along, not 0.2, and the desk is a Blender render of the class the row explicitly accepts, on a row whose named subjects do not include it. Third, the search chip covers thread text in 84 of 300 frames rather than 171 - real, and half as frequent. Since the hand and the desk are the two findings the material critic gives for holding that row at its floor rather than above it, and one is wrong and the other overstated on a surface the row does not name, 22 out of 25 is not a score that survives this pass.

Both blocking findings survive, but not in the shape they were written. The refused-message dead end was true of the tree the critic read and is fixed in the tree now - `send it again` is the first item in the note menu, `spine.sendAgain` puts the event back in the outbox, and a test named for it exists, all landing at 00:14 on the ninth, ten minutes after the last report closed; no artifact has been re-shot, so the still still shows the old build. The silent phone is worse than reported. It is not that the evidence fails to prove a notification: I ran the harness's own path and the build's own service worker records nothing while a minimal one records a notification, because sw.js:121-122 passes `silent: true` alongside `vibrate:` and Chromium refuses that combination outright. Every arrival whose treatment is `interrupt` - the default, and what Settings shows for a feeling - is silently dropped inside the push handler. That is a two-line defect, it is the mechanism behind a blocking finding, six critics wrote about the symptom and none found it, and the reason is structural: no rubric row owns the push path, exactly as no rubric row owns the shared-life modules that are a third of the stated mission. Those two holes, not any individual report, are what this review is missing.

One last thing, which is about the review rather than the build. I could not re-run the code critic's suite result: on the tree as it stood while I worked the suite came back +152 -1 with the scroll test timing out after twenty-five minutes, and by the time it finished that test file had been edited again, two evidence files had been rewritten a second time, and the four dirty .dart files had been committed. The tree moved under the code critic, it moved under me, and evidence/logs/reception_scene.json was rewritten while I had it open. A review whose subject is being edited while it is read cannot say what it scored, and three of the six reports also record a task list or a sibling report surfacing unbidden in their session. The isolation the briefing depends on is leaking at both ends.
